removed_sentences.text: The base model of the Transformer architecture employs a multi-head attention mechanism, where each attention head allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces, as stated in claim IDs C2, C3, and C6.
In multi-head attention, this allows the model to attend to different positions in the input sequence simultaneously with multiple sets of learned projections, supported by claim IDs C3 and C2.
Each attention head in the multi-head mechanism outputs a vector that is concatenated and projected back into the model dimension, as illustrated in claim IDs C5 and C2.
Using multiple attention heads can also lead to redundancy, as there is no mechanism to ensure unique behaviors across different heads, which is noted in claim ID C7.
